sections.text: This final checkpoint is a small program that uses ideas from many units. A command line becomes an enum with a parser, as in the capstone lessons (A command-line tool, A text adventure). Failures are values of a custom error type. You write the From impl for it (Custom error types, Traits), and ? uses it (Unit 6). Stock lives in a HashMap (Unit 5), and the report is built with an iterator pipeline (Unit 8). The checks in main use assert_eq! (Unit 9). You write one trait impl and three functions.

The starter compiles, but four pieces are missing: the From impl, and three bodies marked todo!(), a placeholder that panics with "not yet implemented" when it runs. The compiler shows warnings about unused items until you are done. That is expected. The types, the Display text of each error, run_line and main are written for you. A HashMap has no fixed order, so report must sort the names before it prints them. The program prints each command from a script and its result, so you can see every step.

From: the impl block has the shape impl From<ParseIntError> for StockError, with one function, fn from(_: ParseIntError) -> StockError (the _ means the error value is not used). See the From example in Custom error types. parse: split the line with split_whitespace(), and take the first three words with next(). Then match on the tuple (verb, item, amount), as parse did in the text adventure. An arm like ("add", Some(item), Some(amount)) can call amount.parse()? straight inside Command::Add(...), because your From impl turns the error into StockError::BadNumber. A pattern like "add" | "remove" matches either word.

apply: for Add, use *stock.entry(item).or_insert(0) += amount. Make the message before you move item into entry. For Remove, read the count with *stock.get(&item).unwrap_or(&0). If it is smaller than the amount, return Err(StockError::NotEnough { item, have, wanted: amount }). Otherwise store have - amount with insert. report: collect the keys into a Vec, sort it, filter out the names whose count is 0, then map each to "name=count" and join them with ", ".

Signatures to match: impl From<ParseIntError> for StockError, parse(line: &str) -> Result<Command, StockError>, apply(stock: &mut HashMap<String, u32>, command: Command) -> Result<String, StockError> and report(stock: &HashMap<String, u32>) -> String. Rules worth checking: a missing item or amount is MissingArgument, a bad amount is BadNumber (even when the item is there), an empty line is UnknownCommand(""), add and remove always store the new count (even 0), and items with count 0 do not appear in the report.

exercise.prompt:
Finish the stock keeper. One impl is missing and three bodies are marked todo!().

(1) Write impl From<ParseIntError> for StockError. Its function fn from(_: ParseIntError) -> StockError returns StockError::BadNumber. The _ in place of a name means that the value is not used, which avoids an unused-variable warning. The use line for ParseIntError is already there. This is what lets ? turn a failed parse into a StockError.

(2) fn parse(line: &str) -> Result<Command, StockError> reads the first three words of the line. Commands are written in lower case (Add is not a command). Words after the amount are ignored, and so are words after report. report gives Command::Report. add ITEM AMOUNT gives Command::Add(item, amount), and remove ITEM AMOUNT gives Command::Remove(item, amount). The amount is a u32. If add or remove has no item or no amount, return StockError::MissingArgument. If the amount cannot be parsed as a u32 (for example lots or -5), return StockError::BadNumber (your From impl lets ? do this). Any other first word, or an empty line, gives StockError::UnknownCommand with that first word (an empty text for an empty line).

(3) fn apply(stock: &mut HashMap<String, u32>, command: Command) -> Result<String, StockError>. Add raises the count (a new item starts at 0) and returns the text added AMOUNT ITEM. Remove lowers the count and returns removed AMOUNT ITEM. If there are fewer than AMOUNT in stock (an unknown item counts as 0), it changes nothing and returns StockError::NotEnough { item, have, wanted }. When add or remove succeeds, it always stores the new count in the map, even when it is 0. Report returns report(stock). You may assume that counts fit in a u32.

(4) fn report(stock: &HashMap<String, u32>) -> String lists the items whose count is above 0, sorted by name, as name=count separated by a comma and a space (for example apple=8, pear=2). If there are none, it returns (empty).

Do not change main. When the functions work, main prints:

parse checks passed
> "report"
(empty)
> "add apple 5"
added 5 apple
> "add pear 2"
added 2 pear
> "add apple 3"
added 3 apple
> "remove pear 2"
removed 2 pear
> "remove apple 10"
error: only 8 apple in stock, wanted 10
> "remove kiwi 1"
error: only 0 kiwi in stock, wanted 1
> "add plum"
error: missing item or amount
> "add plum lots"
error: the amount must be a whole number
> "sell apple 1"
error: unknown command 'sell'
> ""
error: unknown command ''
> "report"
apple=8

tests.label: report is parsed as Command::Report
tests.code: check_eq!(parse("report"), Ok(Command::Report));

tests.label: add ITEM AMOUNT is parsed as Command::Add
tests.code: check_eq!(parse("add apple 5"), Ok(Command::Add(String::from("apple"), 5)));

tests.label: An unknown first word gives UnknownCommand with that word
tests.code: check_eq!(parse("sell apple 1"), Err(StockError::UnknownCommand(String::from("sell"))));

tests.label: add without an amount gives MissingArgument
tests.code: check_eq!(parse("add plum"), Err(StockError::MissingArgument));

tests.label: An amount that is not a number gives BadNumber
tests.code: check_eq!(parse("add plum lots"), Err(StockError::BadNumber));

tests.label: Add stores the count and returns a message
Remove with too little stock gives NotEnough and changes nothing
report lists the items sorted by name
remove ITEM AMOUNT is parsed as Command::Remove
tests.code:
check_eq!(parse("remove pear 2"), Ok(Command::Remove(String::from("pear"), 2)));
check_eq!(parse("remove kiwi 0"), Ok(Command::Remove(String::from("kiwi"), 0)));

tests.label: add with other values
tests.code:
check_eq!(parse("add banana 120"), Ok(Command::Add(String::from("banana"), 120)));
check_eq!(parse("add fig 0"), Ok(Command::Add(String::from("fig"), 0)));

tests.label: Words after the amount are ignored
tests.code:
check_eq!(parse("add apple 5 and some more"), Ok(Command::Add(String::from("apple"), 5)));
check_eq!(parse("remove pear 2 please"), Ok(Command::Remove(String::from("pear"), 2)));

tests.label: Words after report are ignored
tests.code:
check_eq!(parse("report now please"), Ok(Command::Report));
check_eq!(parse("report 5"), Ok(Command::Report));

tests.label: add or remove with no item
tests.code:
check_eq!(parse("add"), Err(StockError::MissingArgument));
check_eq!(parse("remove"), Err(StockError::MissingArgument));

tests.label: remove with no amount
tests.code: check_eq!(parse("remove pear"), Err(StockError::MissingArgument));

tests.label: A negative amount is a bad number
tests.code:
check_eq!(parse("add apple -5"), Err(StockError::BadNumber));
check_eq!(parse("remove apple -1"), Err(StockError::BadNumber));

tests.label: A fraction or a number that is too large is a bad number
An empty line gives UnknownCommand with an empty text
tests.code: check_eq!(parse(""), Err(StockError::UnknownCommand(String::from(""))));

tests.label: Commands must be lower case
tests.code:
check_eq!(parse("Add apple 5"), Err(StockError::UnknownCommand(String::from("Add"))));
check_eq!(parse("REPORT"), Err(StockError::UnknownCommand(String::from("REPORT"))));

tests.label: Another unknown word
tests.code:
check_eq!(parse("buy pear 2"), Err(StockError::UnknownCommand(String::from("buy"))));
check_eq!(parse("reports"), Err(StockError::UnknownCommand(String::from("reports"))));

tests.label: Add raises an existing count
A new item starts at 0
Adding 0 still stores the item
Remove lowers the count
Removing everything stores 0
An unknown item counts as 0 and stays unknown
One short of the amount wanted
Removing 0 of an unknown item succeeds and stores 0
Report returns the report
No items give (empty)
tests.code:
let mut stock: ::std::collections::HashMap<String, u32> = ::std::collections::HashMap::new();
check_eq!(report(&stock), "(empty)");

tests.label: Items with a count of 0 are left out
Many items, sorted by name
A whole session through run_line

hints: Do the From impl first, since it lets ? turn a failed parse into your error. Then write parse, apply and report. parse matches on the first three words. report must sort the names and skip counts of 0.

The impl is impl From<ParseIntError> for StockError with fn from(_: ParseIntError) -> StockError. In parse, split the line with split_whitespace() and take verb, item and amount with next(). Use unwrap_or("") for verb.

Match on (verb, item, amount). Arms in order: ("report", _, _), then add and remove with Some(item), Some(amount) and Command::Add(item.to_string(), amount.parse()?), then ("add" | "remove", _, _) for MissingArgument, and last _ for UnknownCommand(verb.to_string()).

quiz.question: Why does parse return Result<Command, StockError> instead of calling panic! on a bad line?
options: Because panic! cannot be used in a function that returns a value
A mistyped command is normal input, not a bug, so the caller gets an error value it can handle
Because Result is always faster than panic!

quiz.question: What does amount.parse()? do inside parse when amount is the text lots?
options: It returns Err(StockError::BadNumber) from parse, because the From impl converts the ParseIntError

quiz.question: Why does report sort the names before it prints them?
options: A HashMap does not promise any order, so sorting makes the output the same on every run
sort removes the names that appear twice
A HashMap cannot be printed in any other way
